data.claim: ddflow bug fixed records could-not-run (closing the bug unverified) when the bug's own auto-filed fix task is unclaimed but the actual fix lives in the worktree of the item the bug was found on
data.falsifier: a scenario where the found item works in a worktree but the bug also has its own unclaimed fix task would be recorded 'verified', not could-not-run
data.mechanism: _fixing_item returns CM.fix_task_for (the bug's own unclaimed fix task) before it ever consults rec.item; _verify_regression then finds fx.worktree empty and records could-not-run, never looking at the found item's worktree that actually holds the fix
data.question: Why does bug fixed record could-not-run when the fix is in the found item's worktree?

evidence.note: R989bfcd1fc CONFIRMED: _fixing_item returns the bug's own unclaimed fix task before consulting rec.item, so _verify_regression finds no worktree and records could-not-run; the found item's worktree (which holds the fix) is never consulted

chunk_findings.detail: The fix still does not implement the “current worktree” part of the stated bug. `_fixing_item(st, cfg, bug_id)` only considers the bug’s own fix task and `rec.item`; it has no access to, and never looks up, the worktree from which `ddflow bug fixed` was invoked. In the reported case, `ddflow bug fixed B-modularity-guard-substring-family ... --mutation-file ...` is run from the ADP-fs worktree that holds the fix. If that ADP-fs item is not `rec.item`, or `rec.item` has no qualifying worktree/landing pair, the function returns the unclaimed `fix_task` (or the wrong `rec.item` item), `_verify_regression` is never pointed at the current ADP-fs worktree, and the mutation is never applied. The added test only covers `bug found --item T1` with the fix in T1’s own worktree, so `rec.item` is the item that carries the fix; it does not exercise the current-worktree-distinct-from-found-item case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/bug_close.py:_fixing_item
